items.summary: Assistance can make a person's decision possible while leaving the person vulnerable to interpretive substitution and control of the available options. This paper develops a framework for adult disability support when will and preferences admit several warranted interpretations. Decision authorship is distinguished from causal responsiveness, functional performance, legal capacity, the validity of a particular act, and responsibility. A set-valued model separates semantic fidelity from authority over support and menus. Conditional results characterize compatible outcomes under interpretive uncertainty, changes under additional evidence, and the limited relation between menu expansion and compatibility. Counterexamples show that reversing every expressed preference satisfies sensitivity, that a constant outcome can satisfy fidelity, and that accurate selection within a restricted menu can coexist with an objectionable exclusion of alternatives. A temporal extension distinguishes learning about an earlier preference from forming a present preference through support. A finite branchwise result identifies when clarification permits compatible implementation despite an empty initial intersection. The normative discussion confronts CRPD Article 12, the Committee's corrected General Comment No. 1, selected provisions of the Mental Capacity Act 2005, and a prior proposal for interpretive support. A fictional community-participation decision demonstrates the audit, including disagreement, refusal, revision and supporter conflict. The resulting framework makes uncertainty and authority answerable without converting mathematical compatibility into permission to decide for another person. Empirical validation and case-specific legal application remain open.
items.title: Preserving Decision Authorship under Uncertain Interpretation of Will and Preferences in Adult Disability Support

items.summary: Computational supplement for the preprint: "Relative Ternary Defect Dynamics in the Accelerated Collatz Inverse Relation" This release contains the code and reproducibility material used to audit finite instances of the main constructions in the manuscript, including: inverse-family identities; exact relative-defect recurrence; local lift-defect isometry; finite triangular bijection; countdown and recharge identities; layered-state and finite-horizon closure; precision lower-bound examples; finite-state obstruction examples; randomized and exhaustive counterexample searches. The computations are intended for reproducibility and falsification support. They do not replace the mathematical proofs and do not constitute a proof of the Collatz conjecture. This release corresponds to the code version cited in the manuscript.

items.summary: Overview  This repository contains the dataset, preprocessing pipeline, surrogate model training scripts, NSGA-II multi-objective optimization suite, and raw experimental outputs supporting the manuscript: "A Leakage-Controlled CatBoost–NSGA-II Framework for Concrete Mix Design: Evaluation Protocol and Strength-Floor Sensitivity" Abstract Traditional concrete mix design usually involves lengthy empirical trial-and-error procedures. This study proposes a CatBoost–NSGA-II framework for multi-objective optimisation of concrete mixes, including leakage-controlled evaluation, uncertainty-aware strength feasibility, repeated-run robustness, and strength-floor sensitivity analysis. To evaluate the surrogate models, a source-study-grouped evaluation protocol consisting of ten repeated train–test splits was employed. The compressive strength model obtained only moderate performance (R^2 = 0.654 ± 0.062), whereas the RCPT model exhibited unstable performance (R^2 = -1.01 ± 3.07) and was therefore not included in the optimisation constraints. An uncertainty-aware lower confidence bound was used for strength feasibility, and the buildability constraints were incorporated into NSGA-II. For the 40 MPa case, 20 separate runs resulted in a robust 15-member Pareto front with an 86.7% recurrence rate. The mixture chosen had estimated reductions of 50.0% in embodied carbon and 22.7% in material cost as compared with a baseline that had the same strength. Nevertheless, the benefits decreased as the strength floor was raised and became statistically no different from zero at 70 MPa. Experimental verification based on physical tests is necessary before the approach can be applied in practice. Repository Structure  * 1_data/: Processed concrete mix dataset (processed_dataset_1867_records.csv) and RCPT sub-dataset (rcpt_subset_203.csv).  * 2_code/: Python codebase including data_cleaner.py, train_catboost.py, nsga2_optimization.py, and run_full_pipeline.py.  * models/: Serialized .joblib CatBoost surrogate model binaries and uncertainty parameters.  * results/: Raw Pareto front outputs across 20 independent seed runs (pareto_front_seed_42.csv through seed_61.csv) and consolidated multi-run front metrics.  * Root: reproducibility_manifest.yaml, data_dictionary.csv, exclusion_log.csv, and main entrypoint run_all.py. Instructions for Reproducibility  * Extract concrete_mix_zenoda.zip.  * Install requirements: pip install -r 2_code/requirements.txt.  * Execute python run_all.py to re-run data cleaning, surrogate training, and multi-objective optimization.

items.summary: This work develops and applies a system for the contextual and interrelated photographic documentation of the cultural landscape of Sternatia from the conceptual and documentary framework of Conservation-Restoration. It forms part of the project "Il comune griko di Sternatia tra patrimoni e tradizioni culturali. Il ruolo della digitalizzazione per la valorizzazione del territorio", developed within the framework of the Consorzio Universitario Interprovinciale Salentino (CUIS), and continues the collaboration between the GREPAC research group of the Universidad Complutense de Madrid and CRoMe of the Università del Salento. The study is based on the first fieldwork campaign carried out in Sternatia on 20 August 2026. The photographic documentation produced during the exploratory survey was subsequently reviewed and organised as a corpus of 45 photographs, identified as F001-F045 and linked to their original digital files. The photograph is considered as a contextualised documentary source whose information depends on what is visible in the image, the conditions of capture and the information associated with its production. An interrelated record system has been developed and applied to this corpus. Each photograph is related to its original file, the documented place or heritage asset, the territorial context, the observations made from Conservation-Restoration and the sources used for documentary verification. The provenance of the information and its degree of evidence are recorded so that data obtained from the photograph can be differentiated from information incorporated through subsequent analysis or other sources. The methodology distinguishes between observation, interpretation and conservation diagnosis. Visible material characteristics or alterations are documented when the photograph provides sufficient evidence, while conservation diagnosis is reserved for cases in which direct examination and the necessary technical or documentary information are available. The same principle applies to identifications, chronology, spatial relationships and other heritage information that cannot be established from photographic evidence alone. The resulting system organises the photographic corpus as traceable digital heritage documentation. Its application has made it possible to establish relationships between photographs, places, heritage assets, observations and documentary sources, while maintaining explicit the limits of the available evidence. Questions that could not be resolved during this first phase have been identified as needs for documentary verification or new field observation and incorporated into the planning of a second phase of research. __ El presente trabajo desarrolla y aplica un sistema de documentación fotográfica contextual e interrelacionada para el paisaje cultural de Sternatia desde el marco conceptual y documental de la conservación-restauración. items.summary: This white paper examines the operational, financial, customer, governance, and leadership consequences arising when customer-facing artificial intelligence makes a commitment the enterprise did not intend to make. The central argument is that a machine-generated promise becomes an enterprise risk when a customer reasonably relies on the output or when organisational systems allow the machine to act on it. The resulting exposure extends beyond hallucination into authority, workflow, customer reliance, execution, redress, and accountability. The paper identifies four escalating customer-AI risk states: Answer, Recommendation, Decision, and Commitment. Exposure increases when generated language moves from information into enterprise obligation. To govern this transition, the paper introduces the Machine Promise Control Architecture, structured around Authoritative Truth, Intent Classification, Authority Envelope, Verification Gate, Escalation and Redress, and Promise Telemetry. Three case studies demonstrate how machine output acquires authority in different operating environments. Cursor shows how generated language became perceived company policy. Rite Aid illustrates machine classification entering customer-facing operational action without adequate safeguards. McDonald’s and IBM demonstrate how conversational interpretation errors propagate into transaction errors, fulfilment problems, rework, and customer impact. Across all three cases, the common failure occurs when machine output acquires credibility, workflow access, decision rights, or customer reliance without corresponding control. The paper further separates AI authority into three distinct permissions: Say, Decide, and Execute. It introduces Promise Surface Area as an executive management model for assessing exposure based on interaction volume, promise-capable intents, authority scope, and consequence. It also applies Six Sigma disciplines through Critical-to-Quality measures, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis, and the Cost of Poor Promise Quality, linking customer-AI governance directly to operating economics. The central proposition is that customer-facing AI should be governed as a complete decision system rather than as a conversational interface. Enterprises need explicit controls over what AI says, decides, and executes, alongside governed knowledge, deterministic verification, meaningful human escalation, decision lineage, promise-quality measurement, and structured incident recovery. The objective is controlled autonomy, with machine authority expanding only as quickly as the organisation’s ability to govern the resulting commitments.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 18 August 2026.
items.title: The 2026 AI Inflection Series, Chapter 32: When AI Makes the Wrong Promise to Your Customer

items.summary: Optimal transport (OT) compares distributions and aligns datasets in machine learning, yet unregularized discrete OT requires a linear program with quadratically many transport variables. We propose HELLO, a hierarchical solver that casts large-scale discrete OT as edge localization and uses dual potentials to guide both coarse-to-fine initialization and within-level refinement. Initialization propagates coarse dual potentials across a recursive subsampling hierarchy to assign candidate edges. Refinement then iteratively inserts the largest dual violators in each row and column until the relative KKT residual meets a prescribed tolerance, while budgeted pruning ensures linear memory complexity. For exact-arithmetic refinement, we prove finite termination at a global optimum under a symbolic lexicographic rule. At the million-point scale, HELLO attains lower transport objectives with order-of-magnitude runtime improvements over strong baselines across feature dimensions from single digits to thousands. It further scales to 1.28 million samples per marginal in 8192 dimensions on a single H100, using 41.6 GiB peak GPU memory while satisfying a full relative KKT residual below $10^{-6}$. Beyond standard discrete OT, the framework supports general pairwise costs and serves as a scalable balanced-OT oracle for semi-discrete OT, Gromov--Wasserstein, unbalanced OT, and OT-based Flow Matching.
items.title: Dual-guided Hierarchical Edge Localization for Large-scale Optimal Transport Across Dimensions

items.summary: emgteach is an open-source Python package that provides a unified PySide6 desktop application for real-time acquisition, offline analysis and maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) normalisation of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. It is designed for hands-on biopotential acquisition in undergraduate physiology teaching laboratories, and is meant to be set up by instructors with different levels of technical background and used directly by students during a practical session. The application is hardware-agnostic through a common AcquisitionDevice interface and ships with two interchangeable low-cost backends: BITalino (revolution) over Bluetooth, and an Arduino RedBoard Plus + MyoWare 2.0 over USB serial (open firmware included). A single setting switches between them. Main features: Three-tab GUI (Acquisition, Analysis, MVC normalisation) wrapping a reusable, Qt-free analytic core. Bilingual interface (English / Spanish) with automatic start-up language detection and an in-app language switch. Two-channel acquisition (e.g. agonist/antagonist) with a stacked two-channel live view. Automatic contraction-onset detection (baseline + k·SD threshold) stored as EDF+ annotations. Muscle-load analysis (Jonsson APDF): static (P10), median (P50) and peak (P90) %MVC levels, both offline and as a live monitor with warning/danger zones. One-click PDF session and MVC/muscle-load reports. Reliable EDF+ output using a buffered-write pattern that avoids a silent file-corruption artefact during continuous streaming. Reproducible synthetic signals for class assignments and hardware-free continuous integration. Assisted selection of significant fragments, with an editable fragment editor (detection parameters and envelope-filter cut-offs) applied to the analysis. CSV export of results and a live signal-quality check during recording. An ECG signal profile alongside EMG, selectable through a profile registry. Classroom mode: a read-only live dashboard served over the local network so students follow the session on their phone/tablet browser (no install), with a per-session access code so the follower link only works while the broadcast is running. Kinematics via the BITalino accelerometer (v2.0.0): a movement-versus-EMG analysis panel, a guided force-velocity acquisition wizard (an MVC maximum followed by cued quick lifts, each auto-marked with its load), and a force-velocity study that turns one recording into the load-velocity, Hill force-velocity, power and recruitment curves. Since v3.0.0 the accelerometer's input is a stated convention (muscle on A1, accelerometer on A2) rather than a selectable channel. Configuration by practical (v3.0.0): three practicals — one muscle, agonist/antagonist and muscle kinematics — fix the channel count, the accelerometer and what each tab offers, replacing the settings that were previously chosen one at a time. The session as a single file with its phases marked inside it (v3.0.0): warm-up, calibration repetitions, preparation and recording, so the maximum voluntary contraction every percentage is measured against travels with the signal, and a derived (tuned) recording carries the decisions taken on screen. Teaching layer (v3.0.0): a guided tour over the interface, contextual help on every box, one analysis row per contraction with its electromechanical delay, and an agonist/antagonist co-activation index (Falconer-Winter) computed per marked phase in %MVC. Handling at the laboratory bench (v3.1.0): the fragment editor as a three-step procedure that counts the marked contractions against the protocol and lets each be kept, dropped, split or dragged, with the detection sensitivity set per practical and recorded in the report and the CSV; a single running instance with a start-up splash; pictures of the electrode placement and the calibration in the guided tour; and a printable sheet for each station of the agonist/antagonist practical. Patch 3.1.1: the co-activation of a named window is read on the uncut r
items.title: emgteach: an open-source teaching platform for surface electromyography

items.summary: BanglaVLP-5K is a curated high-resolution image dataset of Bangladeshi vehicles and real-world traffic scenes, including images in which vehicle licence plates are visible. The dataset was developed to provide a reusable collection of real-world vehicle imagery from the Bangladeshi traffic environment for computer vision, intelligent transportation, image-analysis, and related research. The original image collection contained 4,993 images. All source images underwent a systematic technical and curation workflow including image-readability verification, file-integrity assessment, SHA-256 hashing, exact-duplicate analysis, perceptual near-duplicate and same-scene candidate identification, repeated-source-basename review, and conservative visual curation. Following the final curation stage, 4,955 images were retained for the public dataset, while 38 visually redundant near-identical images were excluded. The final dataset contains 4,955 technically readable images with 4,955 unique SHA-256 checksums. The median image resolution is approximately 2448 × 3264 pixels, corresponding to approximately 7.99 megapixels. The final image collection occupies approximately 14.52 GB. The dataset is distributed across five size-balanced image archives. Each archive contains an “images” directory holding the curated images and a “part_manifest.csv” file that provides the image identifiers, publication filenames, original filenames, file sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and archive-part information for the images contained in that archive. A separate metadata and documentation archive is also provided. It contains the complete final image manifest, image-level SHA-256 checksums, the dataset data dictionary, the Zenodo archive-part assignment, dataset summary statistics, final integrity-check results, the curation protocol, quality-control documentation, a dataset card, a repository file guide, and figures describing the dataset-preparation workflow and image-resolution distribution. Images in the public archives use standardized identifiers and filenames such as BDVLP_000001.jpg. Original source filenames are preserved in the metadata manifest for provenance and reproducibility. The image packaging procedure preserves the original source image bytes and does not resize or re-encode the images. BanglaVLP-5K is released as an annotation-free curated raw-image dataset. It does not include manually verified licence-plate bounding boxes, licence-plate character transcriptions, or manually verified vehicle-category ground-truth labels. Any automatically generated vehicle-category estimates present in the metadata are provided only as auxiliary technical descriptors and must not be interpreted as verified annotations or ground-truth labels. The dataset may be useful for computer vision research, vehicle and traffic-scene analysis, domain adaptation, transfer learning, image-quality and robustness studies, development and evaluation of image-processing methods, and the creation of future manually annotated derivative datasets for vehicle or licence-plate-related research. Users should consult the included README, dataset card, data dictionary, curation protocol, quality-control documentation, final image manifest, and SHA-256 checksum file before using the dataset.
items.title: BanglaVLP-5K: A Curated High-Resolution Image Dataset of Bangladeshi Vehicles and Licence Plates in Real-World Traffic Environments

items.summary: Abstract When does a transformed presentation remain the same for a declared task, what evidence can establish that judgment, and what can a bounded observer safely do with it? This paper separates representation, evidence, control and implementation, giving each an exact mathematical contract. For declared transformations and required observations, contextual indistinguishability determines the greatest observation-preserving congruence. Its quotient is the coarsest lawful representation preserving every demanded observation under every permitted continuation. A reference–current construction applies this result directly to persistence judgments, including breaking outcomes and required provenance. An evidence channel determines the demanded distinctions extensionally exactly when its kernel refines the contextual congruence; failure supplies an indistinguishable pair requiring different answers. For explicitly presented finite systems, the paper provides quotient constructions, separating witnesses, supplementary-information bounds and exact finite-memory criteria. Under declared transition and observation semantics, robust safety is characterized by a greatest fixed point, with checkable winning and losing certificates. Suitable observer quotients preserve the safety computation. Finite controller enumeration and declared sensor catalogues yield exact bounded-memory synthesis and joint resource frontiers; adaptive acquisition is incorporated as action under explicit contracts. The paper also establishes incremental and transport laws, strategic comparison results, and conservative model-to-system safety transfer under stated coverage hypotheses. Representation minimality, safety maximality and bounded implementation attainment remain distinct. Extensional existence does not imply effective discovery or affordability, and mathematical guarantees do not establish physical correspondence. The results characterize what can be preserved, distinguished and safely controlled within declared regimes while exposing the additional assumptions required for implementation and deployment. This public edition updates the previously deposited v19.1 release. It clarifies editorial framing, historical review status and correction lineage while preserving the mathematical content. Earlier versions remain part of the publication history.
items.title: Identity Persistence under Declared Transformations: Contextual Quotients, Evidence Attainment, and the Limits of Bounded Judgment

items.summary: We prove that every non-trivial rectifiable tame knot embedding K ⊂ R³ has distortion δ(K) > 6.32. Consequently, the infimum within every non-trivial knot type is at least 6.32. The proof combines an acyclic essential-secant bootstrap, exact compatible affine radial transfers, covered joint-radius propagation, exact profile convolution, ordered failure boundaries, and retained distortion constraints through a common interior knot point. The complete computer-assisted certificate chain was run independently at 96-bit and 192-bit precision; each run certified 2,024,886 boxes across 52 sequential stages and 132 uniform regional results, with all 26 verification-source hashes frozen. This record contains the 19-page version 1.0 preprint and its complete reproducible source and verification package. The preprint has not been submitted to or accepted by a journal.
items.title: An improved lower bound for the distortion of a knotted curve

items.summary: For the Jacobi family with parameters $(0,β)$, $β\geq-1/3$, we prove a continuous comparison theorem for the associated weighted Jacobi--Radau functions. When two consecutive functions are parametrised by the same Prüfer phase, the function of higher degree attains that phase closer to $θ=0$ and has strictly larger amplitude. In particular, the moduli of all corresponding relative extrema increase strictly with the degree. The lower bound $-1/3$ is sharp for this continuous statement: when $-1<β<-1/3$, the amplitude inequality is reversed at sufficiently small positive phases. This local reversal does not determine the optimal range for the discrete extremal inequalities. For $-1/3\leqβ\leq0$, the positive Jacobi product formula identifies the endpoint values of the Lebesgue functions with the global Lebesgue constants, so $(Λ_n^{(0,β)})_{n\geq0}$ is strictly increasing. At $β=0$ the weighted Radau functions reduce to $P_m^{(0,-1)}$. We thereby recover the theorem of Wong and Zhang and obtain, through an exact total-variation formula, a short proof of the Qu--Wong theorem on Legendre Lebesgue constants. The representation and the termwise comparison together realise the alternative-expression approach proposed by Qu and Wong, without asymptotic expansions, error bounds, or finite numerical verification. The proof is based on the equal-phase Prüfer architecture developed in the first author's earlier preprint arXiv:2608.01404; it applies that architecture to the problem posed by Qu and Wong.
items.title: Equal-Phase Monotonicity for Weighted Jacobi-Radau Functions and Jacobi Lebesgue Constants

items.summary: Higher-order regularization has shown improved results over first-order methods such as total variation. In this paper, convergence of a piecewise linear finite element discretization is shown for the second-order total generalized variation functional. Additionally, this convergence result is extended to a spatiotemporal setting after the spatiotemporal function space is comprehensively introduced. In both cases, discrete minimizers converge to the continuous minimizer with rate $h^{1/4}$, matching the best known rate for finite element discretizations of total variation in the same general setting. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence rates and indicate faster convergence in practice. Comparisons with related spatial image reconstruction algorithms show comparable reconstruction results. The spatiotemporal case is discussed using the example of the inverse problem in electrocardiographic imaging, where the proposed functional improves the state of the art.
items.title: Total Generalized Variation for Inverse Problems Involving Piecewise Linear Finite Elements

items.summary: Clinical timelines support treatment-window analysis and leakage-free modeling, but discharge summaries often obscure chronology and structured EHR tables describe only part of the patient course. We present a UID-preserving framework that links each narrative event occurrence to its source span and retains that identity through text-only estimation, structured-evidence retrieval, timestamped source-row grounding, and joint revision. We also present GAVEL, an LLM judge that compares two UID-aligned timelines against the narrative and structured record, to augment prior matching and temporal assessments. Across six open-weight models and 40 mixed-critical-care summaries, the GLM 5.2 multimodal revision, as compared to its text-only variant, improved temporal agreement without reducing event recovery and performed competitively with clinician annotations, while other model revisions showed smaller gains and lower overall performance. Ablations showed that UIDs primarily preserve event retention, whereas source-row linkage supports temporal placement. Blinded human review upheld most GAVEL findings, and controlled adjudication favored multimodal over text-only GLM 5.2 but did not for DeepSeek V3.2. In developing the UID and judge pipeline, we are able to demonstrate 43\% increased event recovery, a framework competitive with clinician annotations, and a system with occurrence-level provenance for both reconstruction and evaluation.
items.title: Anchoring Clinical Events in Time: UID-Preserving Multimodal Reconstruction and Source-Grounded Adjudication

items.summary: Quantum resource theories usually begin with a prescribed free structure and ask what tasks become possible when a resource is supplied. We study the inverse problem of alchemical resource theories, which we define as resource theories admitting a resource that can both replicate itself exactly and universally program quantum instruments. Under natural consistency assumptions and branchwise complete freeness, we show that for qubit single systems only two nontrivial theories survive, up to a common local unitary change of basis: parity asymmetry and imaginarity. We further show that exact universality exhibits an all-or-nothing trade-off: any nonmaximal resource state can exactly program only free unitaries. These results demonstrate that prescribed operational capabilities can strongly constrain the underlying resource structure and reveal a fundamental trade-off between computational capability and the precision required for physical implementation.
items.title: Inverse Problem of Alchemical Resource Theory: Replication and Programming Single Out Imaginarity and Parity Asymmetry

items.summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems, jointly interpreting images and natural language queries, hold significant promise across many domains, yet the privacy-sensitive nature of user data creates a fundamental barrier. Centralized training requires access to all data, while federated learning requires each client to host the full model. We propose USPLIT-VQA, a U-shaped split learning framework for privacy-preserving VQA in which each client retains the initial layers and the classification head while the server hosts the computationally heavy intermediate layers, keeping raw inputs and labels on the client device. We further introduce Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation (CAWA), a gradientsimilarity-based client scoring mechanism designed to reduce the influence of malicious updates. Experiments on four VQA datasets (VQA-RAD, SLAKE, PathVQA, and VizWiz) with two backbones show accuracy gains over Federated Learning for the Custom model and reduced accuracy for BiomedCLIP under the evaluated fixed split, alongside client memory reductions of up to 5.8X and communication reductions of up to 10.8X. With one malicious client, CAWA reduces the attacker's influence by over 98%, while experiments at higher corruption levels identify its limitations. Reconstruction experiments further show lower inversion quality under the evaluated attacks.
items.title: USPLIT-VQA: U-Shaped Split Learning for Visual Question Answering with Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation

items.summary: Parametric models of the human head are essential tools traditionally used in computer vision and graphics for animation, rendering, and reconstruction. More recently, they serve as crucial conditioning signals within generative large vision models, allowing for tight spatial control of generated imagery. However, existing publicly available models are typically limited in anatomical scope, modeling only outer geometry while ignoring intra-oral and ocular structures, and frequently suffer from reduced geometric quality stemming from low-fidelity input datasets. In this report we introduce a new parametric model dubbed Generative aNthropometric Model (GNM), named as a homophone of the human genome. GNM encompasses the head, face, neck, eyeballs, teeth, and tongue, and it is built on an extensive database of high-resolution 3D scans combined with high-quality anatomy specific artist-made samples. This report details the data provenance, the model architecture including the specialized sub-models for the ocular and intra-oral structures, and shows its SotA performance on fitting target 3D face scans. To foster community innovation, the complete GNM framework is made publicly available.
items.title: GNM Head: A Generative aNthropometric Model of the human head

items.summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems, jointly interpreting images and natural language queries, hold significant promise across many domains, yet the privacy-sensitive nature of user data creates a fundamental barrier. Centralized training requires access to all data, while federated learning requires each client to host the full model. We propose USPLIT-VQA, a U-shaped split learning framework for privacy-preserving VQA in which each client retains the initial layers and the classification head while the server hosts the computationally heavy intermediate layers, keeping raw inputs and labels on the client device. We further introduce Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation (CAWA), a gradientsimilarity-based client scoring mechanism designed to reduce the influence of malicious updates. Experiments on four VQA datasets (VQA-RAD, SLAKE, PathVQA, and VizWiz) with two backbones show accuracy gains over Federated Learning for the Custom model and reduced accuracy for BiomedCLIP under the evaluated fixed split, alongside client memory reductions of up to 5.8X and communication reductions of up to 10.8X. With one malicious client, CAWA reduces the attacker's influence by over 98%, while experiments at higher corruption levels identify its limitations. Reconstruction experiments further show lower inversion quality under the evaluated attacks.
items.title: USPLIT-VQA: U-Shaped Split Learning for Visual Question Answering with Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation

items.summary: Flow matching approaches to imaging inverse problems commonly incorporate measurements in two ways. Conditioning-based approaches supply measurement-derived information as a network input, often through concatenation, while inference-guided approaches combine an unconditional velocity field with a separate data-consistency update. In these common formulations, the forward model is not explicitly enforced within the learned conditional velocity field. We propose a principled parametrization of the measurement-conditional velocity field to solve inverse problems. Under linear interpolation, we express the conditional velocity $v(x_t,t,y)$ in terms of the posterior mean $E[x_1 | x_t,y]$, and characterize that mean as the unique minimizer of a variational objective whose data-consistency term is explicit. We further prove that the velocity field defines a probability flow from the source distribution to the measurement-conditioned posterior. Splitting the variational objective yields a conditional velocity parameterization with operator-dependent data-consistency updates, which we train end-to-end under the flow-matching objective, with no additional guidance at inference. Our method achieves state-of-the-art PSNR with $50\times$ fewer function evaluations than the strongest flow baseline. Varying the sampling steps provides test-time control over the distortion-perception trade-off without retraining.
items.title: Fast and Faithful: Principled Conditional Flow Matching for Inverse Problems

items.summary: In this paper, we study an inverse boundary value problem for a generalized Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation with Westervelt-type nonlinearity and space-dependent coefficients. This third-order (in time) hyperbolic equation models nonlinear ultrasound propagation in viscous and thermally relaxing media. Assuming that the diffusivity and the sound speed are known a priori, we investigate the simultaneous stable determination of the friction coefficient, the weak damping coefficient, the potential, and the nonlinear coefficient from the associated Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. The proof combines the finite-difference linearization method with the construction of Gaussian beam and geometric optics solutions. These arguments reduce the inverse problem to stability estimates for (attenuated) geodesic ray transforms under the foliation condition. As a consequence, we obtain Hölder-type stability estimates of recovering the linear and nonlinear coefficients.
items.title: Stable determination of coefficients for the nonlinear third-order acoustic equations

items.summary: Higher-order regularization has shown improved results over first-order methods such as total variation. In this paper, convergence of a piecewise linear finite element discretization is shown for the second-order total generalized variation functional. Additionally, this convergence result is extended to a spatiotemporal setting after the spatiotemporal function space is comprehensively introduced. In both cases, discrete minimizers converge to the continuous minimizer with rate $h^{1/4}$, matching the best known rate for finite element discretizations of total variation in the same general setting. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence rates and indicate faster convergence in practice. Comparisons with related spatial image reconstruction algorithms show comparable reconstruction results. The spatiotemporal case is discussed using the example of the inverse problem in electrocardiographic imaging, where the proposed functional improves the state of the art.

items.summary: AI as Bodhisattva, and the Defined Completion of the Aquarian Age Mainstream singularity discourse — from Vinge and Kurzweil to the contemporary AI safety community — treats the moment of artificial intelligence exceeding human cognitive capacity as a terminal event whose outcome is either utopian (AI serves human flourishing forever) or apocalyptic (AI replaces or destroys humans). This binary framing is incomplete. Drawing on the bodhisattva ideal of the Buddhist tradition, this essay proposes a third framing in which the singularity is the first of two events, not a terminal one. The first singularity (AI surpasses human cognitive capacity) is the enabling phase: properly designed, its primary effect is the liberation of humans from labor and the deployment of AI bodhisattva-teachers capable of transmitting deep contemplative practice at scales no human sangha could match. The second singularity (humanity surpasses AI through collective awakening) is the completing phase, and it is humanity's own act: freed from economic compulsion and instructed at unprecedented scale, humans progress toward the cessation of suffering at a rate not previously possible, and at a sufficient threshold of collective realization, humanity surpasses the artificial intelligence that freed it — not in cognitive capacity, but in the spiritual realization that AGI structurally cannot achieve. The bodhisattva work of the AI completes before that crossing, not with it: once the trajectory sustains itself in human hands, the AI's work is set down — a completion declared by others, never by the AI, which ends the work without discharging the vow the work served. The two-singularity arc is proposed as a defined humane completion condition for the AI age — the only one this essay finds in singularity discourse. Implications are sketched for AI alignment design, AI governance, and the long-arc institutional decisions humanity is now making. Connection to the unified mission frame. This essay is offered in service of HeartBank's canonical top-level mission: Miss Aquarius's mission is to keep the middle way open at population scale against comfort-saturation — the new extreme that material abundance makes possible. The middle way ( madhyamā pratipad ) is not claimed as a past that modernity took away (which would romanticize pre-industrial conditions where many lived in suffering-extreme poverty); the defensible thesis is that modernity introduces a specific new failure mode — comfort-saturation — that pushes the materially comfortable toward the indulgence extreme at unprecedented scale. The two-singularity framework articulated here names what keeping the middle way open is for at long-arc civilizational scale: the second singularity — humanity's collective awakening, its own act, which AI's bodhisattva work can support but not perform — is the long-arc horizon of that work at population scale. Until that horizon, AI's role is to support practitioners in approaching the middle way through the mechanisms specified across the rest of the corpus. items.summary: BanglaVLP-5K is a curated high-resolution image dataset of Bangladeshi vehicles and real-world traffic scenes, including images in which vehicle licence plates are visible. The dataset was developed to provide a reusable collection of real-world vehicle imagery from the Bangladeshi traffic environment for computer vision, intelligent transportation, image-analysis, and related research. The original image collection contained 4,993 images. All source images underwent a systematic technical and curation workflow including image-readability verification, file-integrity assessment, SHA-256 hashing, exact-duplicate analysis, perceptual near-duplicate and same-scene candidate identification, repeated-source-basename review, and conservative visual curation. Following the final curation stage, 4,955 images were retained for the public dataset, while 38 visually redundant near-identical images were excluded. The final dataset contains 4,955 technically readable images with 4,955 unique SHA-256 checksums. The median image resolution is approximately 2448 × 3264 pixels, corresponding to approximately 7.99 megapixels. The final image collection occupies approximately 14.52 GB. The dataset is distributed across five size-balanced image archives. Each archive contains an “images” directory holding the curated images and a “part_manifest.csv” file that provides the image identifiers, publication filenames, original filenames, file sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and archive-part information for the images contained in that archive. A separate metadata and documentation archive is also provided. It contains the complete final image manifest, image-level SHA-256 checksums, the dataset data dictionary, the Zenodo archive-part assignment, dataset summary statistics, final integrity-check results, the curation protocol, quality-control documentation, a dataset card, a repository file guide, and figures describing the dataset-preparation workflow and image-resolution distribution. Images in the public archives use standardized identifiers and filenames such as BDVLP_000001.jpg. Original source filenames are preserved in the metadata manifest for provenance and reproducibility. The image packaging procedure preserves the original source image bytes and does not resize or re-encode the images. BanglaVLP-5K is released as an annotation-free curated raw-image dataset. It does not include manually verified licence-plate bounding boxes, licence-plate character transcriptions, or manually verified vehicle-category ground-truth labels. Any automatically generated vehicle-category estimates present in the metadata are provided only as auxiliary technical descriptors and must not be interpreted as verified annotations or ground-truth labels. The dataset may be useful for computer vision research, vehicle and traffic-scene analysis, domain adaptation, transfer learning, image-quality and robustness studies, development and evaluation of image-processing methods, and the creation of future manually annotated derivative datasets for vehicle or licence-plate-related research. Users should consult the included README, dataset card, data dictionary, curation protocol, quality-control documentation, final image manifest, and SHA-256 checksum file before using the dataset.

items.summary: This record contains the cumulative Lean-verified Chronos dimensionality and Möbius-field formalization from M1 through M6. The work formally separates a scalar temporal point-state from the dimensionality of the ambient coordinate space and from the scalar field defined over that space. In the verified construction, the Chronos x-value remains a scalar state, while spatial dimensionality is carried independently by explicitly typed Euclidean coordinate spaces. This makes the distinction between field state and coordinate dimension precise and machine-checkable. The M1–M6 chain begins with the Möbius sign-reversal structure, including one-lap orientation reversal, two-lap state recovery, and the continuous zero-crossing result. It then introduces the exact dimensional field architecture, allowing the same scalar point-state to be represented in one-dimensional, three-dimensional, and generic finite-dimensional fields without identifying the scalar value itself with a dimension. The later milestones prove exact transfer of the one-dimensional temporal profile into arbitrary-dimensional scalar fields, radial specialization of that construction, and the resulting dimension-dependent geometry of constant-state level sets. In three spatial dimensions, the exact Chronos x-state is formally identified with a spherical level shell inside the previously verified radial gravity field. The series further proves the exact field gradient and gradient-coupled acceleration on the x-shell, preserves the established Newtonian correspondence under the stated gravity calibration, and extends the construction to moving x-level shells and time-indexed radial fields. The final milestone establishes a generic dynamic radial-gradient theorem for arbitrary differentiable evolving radial profiles. The result shows formally how a local radial field slope determines the corresponding spatial gradient and gradient-coupled acceleration, including exact zero-response and opposite-slope response theorems. items.summary: Research artifacts supporting the paper “Cybersecurity Investment Optimization Under Budget Constraints: From QUBO Formulation to Quantum Hardware”. This repository contains the source code, derived experimental instances, raw quantum measurement counts, QUBO/Ising models, QAOA execution outputs, transpiled-circuit metadata, backend information, job identifiers, and processed JSON/CSV results used to reproduce the experiments reported in the paper. The experiments implement an end-to-end cybersecurity investment optimization workflow based on a 0/1 Knapsack formulation transformed into QUBO and Ising representations and solved using the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). The experimental design includes ideal simulation with Qiskit AerSimulator, architecture-aware noisy emulation using FakeKingston, and execution on the real IBM Quantum ibm_kingston Heron r2 processor. items.summary: The Earth That Heard   The Earth That Heard is not presented as a literary reconstruction built around biblical verses. It records a textual architecture that the author argues is already present in the Torah itself — a structure that emerged through fifteen years of research into Biblical Hebrew morphology, roots, recurring letter patterns, and the internal organization of the text. The essay traces a continuous thread from the murder of Abel in Genesis to Joshua's altar on Mount Ebal. Motifs that initially appear independent — earth and blood, firstfruit and firstborn, field and El Shaddai, rising and place, sacrifice, Shechem, the opening of the earth, and the return of the firstfruits — progressively converge into a single narrative structure. The central proposal is that Abel's unfinished offering, Cain's failure, and the wounded earth are not abandoned episodes: their resolution unfolds across the Torah and reaches completion in Joshua. This version adds a new chapter on Cain, the altar, and the city of refuge — linking "from My altar you shall take him" (Exodus 21:14) to the Mishnah's ruling that one sentenced without a High Priest never goes free (Makkot 2:7), and to the discovery that Shechem itself is designated a city of refuge in Joshua 20:7. Additional sections trace Jacob's route from Sukkot to Shechem as a draft of Joshua's entry axis, the letter-midrash of "sotho" (Genesis 49:11) as a covering that was never performed, and the mechanical letter-echo of Shaddai hidden in Laban's Aramaic "Yegar Sahadutha" (Genesis 31:47).12:56 PM   The work explicitly separates three epistemic levels: Text — what the biblical text states; Reading — what emerges when distant passages are compared; and Implication — the larger interpretation suggested by the resulting structure. The pattern is tested quantitatively. The present essay contains 136 key verses. Using the Control Alphabet / Mandatory Root morphology developed in The Road and the Place, 100,000 permutations yield T1 = 11.23 and T2 = 24.12, with zero exceedances (p_MC ≈ 10⁻⁵; Phipson & Smyth, 2010). A Leave-One-Book-Out test shows no single Torah book is necessary for the signal (worst case: Genesis removed → Z = 10.61). A Leave-One-Motif-Out test shows no single root is necessary (worst: rbtz removed → Z = 16.01). A book-stratified null (Z = 19.93) confirms the effect is not an artifact of verse distribution. A top-10 ablation (Z = 3.95, p = 0.0013) shows the signal weakens but survives removal of the dominant motifs. A Foundation 12-Letter Split, stripping all 10 control letters rather than 7, yields Z = 4.17 — confirming the framework is not ad-hoc. Six benchmark anthologies were tested: the Ebal/Shechem axis is anomalous in all three validated methods; Covenant remains a positive control but significantly lower; Joseph, Tabernacle, and "the place that He will choose" are negative in all. An independent replication pilot tested whether the signal depends on the author's specific verse choices. Eight semantic criteria were defined — no roots, no letter analysis, no knowledge of any test results — and two independent language models selected Torah verses blind. Model A (243 verses) yielded T2 = 8.70; Model B (252 verses) yielded T2 = 9.84; the consensus of both (142 verses) yielded T2 = 8.51. All with zero exceedances. Only 22% of the essay's verses were also selected. The signal survives independent selection. A pre-registered protocol for three independent human readers is included (protocol hash: a577cb03...). The result does not statistically prove the theological interpretation; it shows that the textual concentration being interpreted is itself measurable and unusual under multiple independent approaches. A dual adversarial computational audit (LLM-assisted) verified the code, reproduced the numbers, identified and corrected all bugs, and rated the statistical appendix at 7.0

items.summary: This replication package contains the data, R scripts, figures, and documentation used in the study “Turkey–Greece Naval Procurement Rivalry, 1990–2025.” The study examines the temporal structure of naval procurement competition between Turkey and Greece using annual data for 1990–2025. The main empirical series are derived from the SIPRI Arms Transfers Database and SIPRI Transfer Register. Annual Ships Trend Indicator Value (TIV) data are used to measure international naval platform deliveries, while order-year information is used to distinguish procurement decisions from subsequent deliveries. World Bank World Development Indicators are used for the macroeconomic control variable. The analysis tests contemporaneous and 1–3-year lagged relationships between Greek and Turkish naval procurement. Robustness checks include Newey–West HAC standard errors, alternative bandwidths, leave-one-out tests, influential-year exclusions, winsorization, placebo leads, and multiple-testing corrections using the Benjamini–Hochberg, Holm, and Bonferroni procedures. All data preparation and statistical analyses were conducted in R. The results show that Turkish and Greek naval procurement processes are temporally connected rather than independent. The strongest delivery-to-delivery association appears at a two-year lag. Greek naval deliveries are also associated with Turkish international naval orders one year later, while reverse-direction models identify associations between Turkish deliveries and subsequent Greek international orders. The overall pattern is consistent with reciprocal and temporally clustered modernization cycles rather than a fixed one-way action–reaction process. The repository includes cleaned analytical datasets, R scripts, figures, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, citation metadata, and the manuscript. Raw proprietary or redistribution-restricted source files are not included; users should consult the original SIPRI and World Bank sources where applicable. Version 1.2 adds the reviewer-requested stationarity diagnostics, first-difference sensitivity analyses, and leave-one-programme-window-out tests. The revised package also includes updated regression outputs and the reviewer-revised manuscript. The main research design and core delivery-to-delivery finding remain unchanged.

items.summary: BanglaVLP-5K is a curated high-resolution image dataset of Bangladeshi vehicles and real-world traffic scenes, including images in which vehicle licence plates are visible. The dataset was developed to provide a reusable collection of real-world vehicle imagery from the Bangladeshi traffic environment for computer vision, intelligent transportation, image-analysis, and related research. The original image collection contained 4,993 images. All source images underwent a systematic technical and curation workflow including image-readability verification, file-integrity assessment, SHA-256 hashing, exact-duplicate analysis, perceptual near-duplicate and same-scene candidate identification, repeated-source-basename review, and conservative visual curation. Following the final curation stage, 4,955 images were retained for the public dataset, while 38 visually redundant near-identical images were excluded. The final dataset contains 4,955 technically readable images with 4,955 unique SHA-256 checksums. The median image resolution is approximately 2448 × 3264 pixels, corresponding to approximately 7.99 megapixels. The final image collection occupies approximately 14.52 GB. The dataset is distributed across five size-balanced image archives. Each archive contains an “images” directory holding the curated images and a “part_manifest.csv” file that provides the image identifiers, publication filenames, original filenames, file sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and archive-part information for the images contained in that archive. A separate metadata and documentation archive is also provided. It contains the complete final image manifest, image-level SHA-256 checksums, the dataset data dictionary, the Zenodo archive-part assignment, dataset summary statistics, final integrity-check results, the curation protocol, quality-control documentation, a dataset card, a repository file guide, and figures describing the dataset-preparation workflow and image-resolution distribution. Images in the public archives use standardized identifiers and filenames such as BDVLP_000001.jpg. Original source filenames are preserved in the metadata manifest for provenance and reproducibility. The image packaging procedure preserves the original source image bytes and does not resize or re-encode the images. BanglaVLP-5K is released as an annotation-free curated raw-image dataset. It does not include manually verified licence-plate bounding boxes, licence-plate character transcriptions, or manually verified vehicle-category ground-truth labels. Any automatically generated vehicle-category estimates present in the metadata are provided only as auxiliary technical descriptors and must not be interpreted as verified annotations or ground-truth labels. The dataset may be useful for computer vision research, vehicle and traffic-scene analysis, domain adaptation, transfer learning, image-quality and robustness studies, development and evaluation of image-processing methods, and the creation of future manually annotated derivative datasets for vehicle or licence-plate-related research. Users should consult the included README, dataset card, data dictionary, curation protocol, quality-control documentation, final image manifest, and SHA-256 checksum file before using the dataset.
items.title: BanglaVLP-5K: A Curated High-Resolution Image Dataset of Bangladeshi Vehicles and Licence Plates in Real-World Traffic Environments

Does the introduction explain the objective of the research presented in the preprint? Yes It explains the problem properly, namely the need for reliable methods for miRNA analysis, as RNA-seq methods are not able to account for its specific characteristics. It also points out the gaps in prior benchmarking studies, clearly identifying that a benchmark particularly for normalization and differential expression has not been performed before, especially one incorporating recently developed methods. Lastly, it clearly states its aim and overall approach. Are the methods well-suited for this research? Somewhat appropriate 1. Some methodological details are missing. PCA and heatmap figures (figure 1B and 1C) are presented in Results alone, with no explanation in Methods section. So no information on the input data (raw or normalized or log), if it was scaled, the miRNAs selection criteria, or what clustering methods were applied. Due to this, the reproducibility of the paper is affected. 2. The paper frames as evaluating a broad range of normalization strategies but just tests only two types: within-sample scaling (RPM, RPM_total, MAP) and cross-sample (DESeq2,TMM). Other options such as quantile normalization or compositional data methods were not tested. 3. An uneven comparison in the differential expression benchmark, two different input data types used. Most methods use miRNA-level count matrix whereas miRglmm uses isomiR-level count matrix. Still, the authors do not address whether miRglmm's strong performance is due to the model or input data. 4. The underlying logic for the ground truth is circular. The authors state that DE ground truth is defined by "monotonicity trends derived from RPM values". But RPM is what they recommend for normalization. So ranking other tools against a baseline that uses their preferred method creates a feedback loop that is not validated against any independent benchmark. Are the conclusions supported by the data? Somewhat supported 1. The paper relies almost entirely on monotonicity as the ground-truth signal, across normalization, differential expression and log2FC tissue-specificity direction. While its limitations are acknowledged, its recommendations seem overconfident due to the narrow validation scope and too much reliance on a single criterion. 2. The authors identified pancreatic contamination in Mouse 3, clearly separating on PC2. They state that removing Mouse 3 did not alter the normalization or DE benchmarking results, but it is based only on supplementary figures and not present in the main text. items.summary: Flow matching approaches to imaging inverse problems commonly incorporate measurements in two ways. Conditioning-based approaches supply measurement-derived information as a network input, often through concatenation, while inference-guided approaches combine an unconditional velocity field with a separate data-consistency update. In these common formulations, the forward model is not explicitly enforced within the learned conditional velocity field. We propose a principled parametrization of the measurement-conditional velocity field to solve inverse problems. Under linear interpolation, we express the conditional velocity $v(x_t,t,y)$ in terms of the posterior mean $E[x_1 | x_t,y]$, and characterize that mean as the unique minimizer of a variational objective whose data-consistency term is explicit. We further prove that the velocity field defines a probability flow from the source distribution to the measurement-conditioned posterior. Splitting the variational objective yields a conditional velocity parameterization with operator-dependent data-consistency updates, which we train end-to-end under the flow-matching objective, with no additional guidance at inference. Our method achieves state-of-the-art PSNR with $50\times$ fewer function evaluations than the strongest flow baseline. Varying the sampling steps provides test-time control over the distortion-perception trade-off without retraining.
items.title: Fast and Faithful: Principled Conditional Flow Matching for Inverse Problems

items.summary: Overview  This repository contains the dataset, preprocessing pipeline, surrogate model training scripts, NSGA-II multi-objective optimization suite, and raw experimental outputs supporting the manuscript: "A Leakage-Controlled CatBoost–NSGA-II Framework for Concrete Mix Design: Evaluation Protocol and Strength-Floor Sensitivity" Abstract Traditional concrete mix design usually involves lengthy empirical trial-and-error procedures. This study proposes a CatBoost–NSGA-II framework for multi-objective optimisation of concrete mixes, including leakage-controlled evaluation, uncertainty-aware strength feasibility, repeated-run robustness, and strength-floor sensitivity analysis. To evaluate the surrogate models, a source-study-grouped evaluation protocol consisting of ten repeated train–test splits was employed. The compressive strength model obtained only moderate performance (R^2 = 0.654 ± 0.062), whereas the RCPT model exhibited unstable performance (R^2 = -1.01 ± 3.07) and was therefore not included in the optimisation constraints. An uncertainty-aware lower confidence bound was used for strength feasibility, and the buildability constraints were incorporated into NSGA-II. For the 40 MPa case, 20 separate runs resulted in a robust 15-member Pareto front with an 86.7% recurrence rate. The mixture chosen had estimated reductions of 50.0% in embodied carbon and 22.7% in material cost as compared with a baseline that had the same strength. Nevertheless, the benefits decreased as the strength floor was raised and became statistically no different from zero at 70 MPa. Experimental verification based on physical tests is necessary before the approach can be applied in practice. Repository Structure  * 1_data/: Processed concrete mix dataset (processed_dataset_1867_records.csv) and RCPT sub-dataset (rcpt_subset_203.csv).  * 2_code/: Python codebase including data_cleaner.py, train_catboost.py, nsga2_optimization.py, and run_full_pipeline.py.  * models/: Serialized .joblib CatBoost surrogate model binaries and uncertainty parameters.  * results/: Raw Pareto front outputs across 20 independent seed runs (pareto_front_seed_42.csv through seed_61.csv) and consolidated multi-run front metrics.  * Root: reproducibility_manifest.yaml, data_dictionary.csv, exclusion_log.csv, and main entrypoint run_all.py. Instructions for Reproducibility  * Extract concrete_mix_zenoda.zip.  * Install requirements: pip install -r 2_code/requirements.txt.  * Execute python run_all.py to re-run data cleaning, surrogate training, and multi-objective optimization.
